speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces. To understand the cause, have you had any fever, fatigue, or a sore throat recently? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and ESR.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your normal blood work and symptoms of blisters and mucosal ulcers, have you noticed any specific triggers like sunlight exposure, new medications, or contact with certain plants or chemicals? REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of forearm lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mentioned hiking recently but denying poison ivy; have you noticed any new rash or blisters appearing specifically on sun-exposed areas of your arms or face? REQUEST IMAGES: Full-body skin exam focusing on distribution of blisters.

Also, regarding your recent medications, did the blistering or mucosal ulcers start shortly after you began taking captopril?

speaker: Patient
text: includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda. The combination of blistering on sun-exposed skin, mucosal involvement, a family history of porphyrias (pernicious anemia is often confused or co-occurring, but the specific family history clue points to PCT), and recent initiation of captopril (which can inhibit heme synthesis) is highly suggestive. I am requesting images of the lesions to confirm fragility and scarring typical of PCT. REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution photos of forearm blisters showing fragility, bullae, and milia.
